rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the full elution window while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The retention and resolution pattern will guide window trimming and targeted slope or temperature changes.

Change only gradient duration to measure how the unresolved early cluster and borderline later pair respond to slope. This will distinguish slope-sensitive overlaps from pairs needing a temperature or starting-composition change.

The shallower gradient improved the early cluster but introduced a time penalty. Test higher temperature at the original slope to seek a selectivity change that resolves the cluster while keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

At 60 C only one pair remains below target, with ample time before the 10-minute penalty threshold. A shallower gradient tests whether that pair can reach R ≥ 1.5 while retaining the favorable temperature selectivity.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so simply extending the run is unlikely to help. Raise the starting organic fraction to test a different selectivity window while monitoring retention of the first peak.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark and test a shorter gradient. Reducing tG by one grid step may shorten elution while preserving full resolution of the two closest pairs.

Narrow the gradient window to give a slope between injections 5 and 6, aiming to restore both marginal pairs to R ≥ 1.5 while eluting faster than injection 5. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Injection 7 is the fastest fully resolved method so far. Shift its organic window upward at unchanged slope to test whether elution can be shortened further without compressing the early cluster below R = 1.5.

Keep injection 7 as the fastest fully resolved benchmark and explore the opposite temperature extreme for a different selectivity pattern. A broad, relatively steep gradient limits late retention while testing whether cooler conditions separate the early cluster more effectively.

Return near the high-temperature optimum and lower temperature one step from injection 8. This tests whether increased retention and shifted selectivity can rescue its single unresolved pair while remaining faster than injection 7.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 11 to restore its marginal pair above R = 1.5. This trimmed six-minute gradient should retain full resolution, with the last peak expected near the gradient endpoint.

The fastest fully resolved method remains injection 7, but its minimum resolution is only 1.51. Test a shallower gradient for a larger resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes and preserving the maximum CRF.

Reduce the endpoint one step from injection 12 to bring its lone marginal pair above R = 1.5. This should establish another maximum-score method with ample separation of the neighboring pair and a last peak comfortably before 10 minutes.
